import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes (mean difference in outcome groups)
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        group0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
        group1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
        effect_size = np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)
        effect_sizes.append(abs(effect_size))
    
    # Rank features by effect size
    ranked_indices = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1]
    
    # Select top candidates avoiding near-duplicates
    drivers = []
    used_ids = set()
    
    # Build correlation matrix to identify near-duplicates
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    
    for idx in ranked_indices:
        fid = feats.ids[idx]
        if fid in used_ids:
            continue
            
        # Check if this feature is correlated with any already selected driver
        is_duplicate = False
        for d_fid in drivers:
            d_idx = feats.column(d_fid)
            if abs(corr_matrix[idx, d_idx]) >= 0.6:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
                
        if not is_duplicate:
            drivers.append(fid)
            used_ids.add(fid)
            if len(drivers) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
                break
    
    # For products, look for simple interactions between top drivers
    products = []
    if len(drivers) >= 2:
        # Only include interaction if both drivers have strong effects
        if abs(np.mean(feats.x[feats.y == 1, feats.column(drivers[0])]) - 
               np.mean(feats.x[feats.y == 0, feats.column(drivers[0])])) > 0.2:
            products = [(drivers[0], drivers[1])]
    
    # For loadings, use top features with high effect sizes
    loadings = {}
    # Only include drivers in loadings
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if fid in drivers:
            effect_size = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]) - np.mean(feats.x[feats.y == 0, i])
            loadings[fid] = effect_size
    
    # Columns = all features that might contribute to model but keep it small
    columns = list(drivers)  # Only include drivers to keep model small
    
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(drivers),
        columns=tuple(columns),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
